q: Identify this structure: a 1933 Finnish tuberculosis hospital that Alvar Aalto liked to call a 'medical instrument.'
n: Designed by Alvar Aalto around the needs of tuberculosis patients — sunlight, ventilation, and hygiene — it became a basis for contemporary hospital design, therapeutic architecture, and biophilic design.

q: Which two architects designed the Centre Pompidou (Paris, 1977)?
o: Ludwig Mies van der Rohe and Philip Johnson
n: Renzo Piano and Richard Rogers designed the Centre Pompidou, whose 'inside-out' logic — with all services on the exterior — is seen today in modern airports and tech campuses prioritizing flexibility.

q: Identify this structure: a 1931 French villa raised on pilotis with ribbon windows and a rooftop terrace.
n: Designed by Le Corbusier, its concrete slab floors on vertical columns, flat roof, and small ground level beneath the main living quarters manifested the 'Five Points of Architecture.'

q: Identify this structure: a 1952 French high-density housing block described as a 'vertical city,' with modular units and rooftop gardens.
n: Designed by Le Corbusier, this high-density housing block introduced modular units, communal spaces, and rooftop gardens, influencing later urban housing blocks, co-living spaces, and green roofs.

q: Which architect designed the Paimio Sanatorium (Finland, 1933), calling the building a 'medical instrument'?
n: Alvar Aalto designed the Paimio Sanatorium around the needs of tuberculosis patients, integrating furniture, lighting, and color psychology into healing environments.

q: Identify this structure: a 1932 Parisian residence and medical office built with glass blocks, steel, and industrial detailing.
n: Designed by Pierre Chareau and Bernard Bijvoet, it innovatively used glass blocks, steel, and industrial detailing, combining a residence and medical office with mechanized elements.

q: Identify this structure: a pair of bronze-clad 1958 New York office towers set back from the street around an open plaza.
n: Designed by Ludwig Mies van der Rohe and Philip Johnson, this 38-storey tower's open street-front plaza became a common feature of later New York City skyscrapers.

q: Identify this structure: a 1977 Parisian cultural center with its mechanical services — plumbing, electricity, elevators — color-coded and placed on the exterior.
n: Designed by Renzo Piano and Richard Rogers, it turned architecture inside out, pioneering High-Tech architecture and creating massive, flexible interior spaces reconfigurable for any exhibition.

q: Which magazine sponsored the Case Study Houses program (USA, 1945–1966)?
n: Arts & Architecture magazine sponsored the Case Study Houses program, seeking prototype modern homes that could be both easily replicated and readily affordable to the average American.

q: Which architect designed the Guggenheim Museum, Bilbao (Spain, 1997), introducing the 'Bilbao Effect'?
n: Frank Gehry designed the Guggenheim Bilbao, whose success moved architecture into the era of Building Information Modeling (BIM) and toward deconstructivist form-finding.

q: Which architect designed Villa Savoye (France, 1931)?
n: Le Corbusier designed Villa Savoye, whose pilotis, flat roof terrace, open plan, horizontal windows, and free façade manifested his 'Five Points of Architecture,' shifting design toward function over form.

q: Which architect designed the Farnsworth House (Illinois, 1951)?
n: Ludwig Mies van der Rohe designed the Farnsworth House as the residential answer to the Barcelona Pavilion, popularizing glass houses, open interiors, and minimalism.

q: Which two architects designed the Maison de Verre (France, 1932)?
n: Pierre Chareau and Bernard Bijvoet designed the Maison de Verre, whose innovative use of glass blocks, steel, and industrial detailing influenced mixed-use buildings and industrial interior aesthetics.

q: Which two architects designed the Seagram Building (New York, 1958)?
o: Ludwig Mies van der Rohe and Philip Johnson
n: Ludwig Mies van der Rohe and Philip Johnson designed the Seagram Building, an iconic International Style office tower that introduced the steel-and-glass skyscraper with visible structure and a clean grid.

q: Who founded the Bauhaus School (Germany, 1925–1933)?
n: Walter Gropius founded the Bauhaus, which — along with Hannes Meyer and Ludwig Mies van der Rohe — influenced everything from IKEA furniture to modular housing to modern design education.

q: Identify this structure: a 1951 Illinois residence reduced to one floor, a steel frame, and glass curtain walls, with a single terrace overhung to one side.
n: Designed by Ludwig Mies van der Rohe as the residential answer to the Barcelona Pavilion, its open floor plan and glass walls emphasized transparency and connection to nature, exemplifying the International Style.

q: Which architect designed the Unité d'Habitation (France, 1952)?
n: Le Corbusier designed the Unité d'Habitation as high-density housing conceived as a 'vertical city,' introducing modular units and communal spaces.

q: Which architect designed the Salk Institute (California, 1965)?
n: Louis Kahn designed the Salk Institute, whose blend of monumental architecture and scientific function inspired later institutional buildings with meditative spaces, minimalism, and environmental integration.

q: Identify this structure: a German school building (1925–1933) with a glass curtain wall reading 'BAUHAUS' down its façade.
n: Founded by Walter Gropius and also led by Hannes Meyer and Ludwig Mies van der Rohe, the Bauhaus blended architecture, art, and industrial design, prioritizing functionality, simplicity, and mass production.

q: Identify this structure: one of a series of experimental American prototype homes (1945–1966) sponsored by Arts & Architecture magazine, shown here designed by Charles and Ray Eames.
n: Sponsored by Arts & Architecture magazine, this program of experimental post-war housing used industrial materials, prefab methods, and open plans, setting the tone for mid-century modern and suburban home design.

q: Identify this structure: a 1965 California research institute in raw concrete, arranged symmetrically around a central water channel courtyard.
n: Designed by Louis Kahn, it blends monumental architecture with scientific function, showing masterful use of symmetry, natural light, and raw concrete (Brutalism).

q: Identify this structure: a 1997 Spanish museum clad in titanium panels with an explosion of curvilinear, undulating forms.
n: Designed by Frank Gehry, its complex titanium forms were only possible using advanced aerospace software (CATIA), and it introduced the 'Bilbao Effect' — the idea that a single iconic building could revitalize a city's economy.
